transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I've been feeling deeply depressed and sad for about a year and a half now. I just can't seem to shake this heavy mood, and that's really what brings me in today.
During this year and a half, have you ever experienced periods lasting a few days where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or impulsive, to the point where you didn't need much sleep?
No, I've never experienced anything like that at all. In fact, it's been completely the opposite—I feel constantly exhausted, down, and completely lacking in energy.

During this year and a half, have there been any periods of a few weeks or months where your mood lifted and you felt mostly back to your normal self, or has this low mood been present nearly every day for the entire time?

No, there haven't been any breaks or times where I felt back to normal. This low mood has been present nearly every single day for the entire year and a half. It has just been a continuous, persistently heavy feeling that never seems to lift.
To better understand the physical impact of this, have you noticed significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns—such as sleeping too much or too little—since this began?
Honestly, I haven't noticed any major changes in my appetite or sleep patterns. I'm not really sure if they have changed much since this all started.
Since you've been feeling this way, have you struggled with feelings of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or a significant loss of interest in activities you once enjoyed?

Yes, I feel completely useless and find myself constantly feeling guilty and blaming myself for even the smallest daily matters. I've also completely lost interest in the hobbies and activities I used to enjoy, as nothing seems to bring me any pleasure anymore.

Looking back to when this began a year and a half ago, did your symptoms start suddenly after a specific stressful event, or was it more of a gradual decline that you couldn't quite pin to a specific time?
I can't recall any specific stressful event that triggered this. It felt much more like a gradual decline over time that I couldn't quite pin down to a single moment.
On a typical day, would you say your mood is so low that it significantly interferes with your ability to work, attend school, or manage your daily responsibilities?

Yes, it interferes with everything. I have absolutely no motivation to start or finish any tasks, and I feel constantly exhausted both physically and mentally. It has made managing my daily responsibilities feel almost impossible.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a continuous low mood lasting 1.5 years without any periods of remission or hypomanic/manic symptoms. This chronic presentation, exceeding the two-year threshold typically required for Persistent Depressive Disorder (though the patient is at 1.5 years, the clinical picture is highly consistent with chronic depression), makes Persistent Depressive Disorder the primary candidate. I am removing Major Depressive Disorder as the primary focus because the patient describes a persistent, non-remitting state rather than episodic major depressive episodes.
